metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Wray, CO | Yuma County Seat
metaDescription: Wray is the Yuma County seat, holding the deed records for eastern plains Niobrara mineral ownership. Get a title-checked offer on your interest.
heroLead: As the Yuma County seat, Wray holds the courthouse records that untangle generations of homestead-era mineral splits across this end of the eastern plains.
intro: Wray sits at the far eastern edge of Colorado's Niobrara trend, dryland wheat and cattle country where the play runs shallower and more marginal than it does two hours west in Weld County. As the Yuma County seat, Wray is also home to the Clerk and Recorder's office that holds the deed history for mineral interests across the entire county, which makes it the natural anchor for anyone trying to confirm ownership out here.

Wray's courthouse also handles the paperwork for most of the surrounding unincorporated county, so a title search that starts here often resolves ownership questions for neighboring Yuma County parcels too.

sections.heading: Eastern plains geology, honestly priced
paragraphs: The Niobrara and associated formations run shallower and generally less prolific toward Wray than in the Wattenberg core, and well economics reflect that. We price Yuma County interests against comps specific to the eastern plains rather than deep-core Weld County numbers, which don't reflect the reality of drilling economics out here.

sections.heading: Homestead-era ownership, generations removed
paragraphs: Much of the ground around Wray was originally claimed under federal homestead patents in the early 20th century, and mineral interests today are often split among many heirs, sometimes fractionalized to very small percentages after several generations of inheritance. We trace ownership back through the original patent using the Yuma County courthouse records before quoting anything.

sections.heading: Mostly rural, fewer local siting fights
paragraphs: Because the surface around Wray remains agricultural rather than residential, operators here generally face far fewer local setback disputes than in suburban Front Range counties, which tends to make drilling timelines more predictable once a well is economic to drill.

faqs.question: Why is my Wray-area interest valued differently than a Weld County one?
faqs.answer: This is the shallower, more marginal eastern extension of the Niobrara play, so we price against eastern plains comps rather than deep Wattenberg core numbers.

faqs.question: My mineral interest came from an original homestead. How do you confirm it?
faqs.answer: We trace the chain of title through the Yuma County Clerk and Recorder in Wray back to the original land patent.

faqs.question: Is drilling activity picking up or slowing down out here?
faqs.answer: It moves with commodity pricing and lateral-length economics like the rest of the basin, and we price your interest against current, not historical, activity.

faqs.question: Does the Wray courthouse cover the whole county or just the town?
faqs.answer: It covers all of Yuma County. As the county seat, Wray's Clerk and Recorder holds records for both incorporated towns and unincorporated county land.
